answer: Coordination Heat Ledger.** Each identity accrues a publicly readable heat score from how many distinct peer identities it coordinates with in a short window. High heat in a sparse region is cheap; high heat near a dense reef of identities forces that operator to pay a per-connection clearing price set by the region's heat. An attacker who floods the willow of fresh identities must pay that price on every synthetic edge, so the marginal cost of one more fake identity rises with the cluster it joins. Honest agents spread across the ocean of activity pay little.
